bottom_line: In patients with chronic heart failure, n-3 PUFA 1 g daily vs placebo reduced all-cause mortality (adjusted hazard ratio [HR] 0.91 [95.5% CI 0.833–0.998]).
implications: Based on the reported adjusted HRs, n-3 PUFA was associated with small reductions in all-cause mortality (adjusted HR 0.91 [95.5% CI 0.833–0.998]) and in death or cardiovascular hospital admission (adjusted HR 0.92 [99% CI 0.849–0.999]) over a median 3.9 years; gastrointestinal disorders were similar (96 [3%] vs 92 [3%]). These numbers support a modest benefit on these endpoints in this trial population, but do not establish reductions for endpoints where effects were not significant (eg, sudden cardiac death adjusted HR 0.93 [95% CI 0.79–1.08]).

major_points.text: Randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial in Italy enrolling NYHA class II–IV chronic heart failure patients.
major_points.quote: We undertook a randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial in 326 cardiology and 31 internal medicine centres in Italy. We enrolled patients with chronic heart failure of New York Heart Association class II–IV

major_points.text: Patients were randomly assigned to n-3 PUFA 1 g daily or placebo using concealed computerised telephone randomisation.
major_points.quote: randomly assigned them to n-3 PUFA 1 g daily (n=3494) or placebo (n=3481) by a concealed, computerised telephone randomisation system.
Patients were followed up for a median of 3·9 years (IQR 3·0–4·5).

major_points.text: Co-primary endpoints were time to death and time to death or admission for cardiovascular reasons.
major_points.quote: Primary endpoints were time to death, and time to death or admission to hospital for cardiovascular reasons.

major_points.text: All-cause mortality was lower with n-3 PUFA than placebo (955 vs 1014 deaths) with adjusted HR 0.91 (95.5% CI 0.833–0.998).
major_points.quote: 955 (27%) patients died from any cause in the n-3 PUFA group and 1014 (29%) in the placebo group (adjusted hazard ratio [HR] 0·91 [95·5% CI 0·833–0·998], p=0·041).

major_points.text: Composite of death or cardiovascular hospital admission occurred less often with n-3 PUFA than placebo (1981 vs 2053) with adjusted HR 0.92 (99% CI 0.849–0.999).
major_points.quote: 1981 (57%) patients in the n-3 PUFA group and 2053 (59%) in the placebo group died or were admitted to hospital for cardiovascular reasons (adjusted HR 0·92 [99% CI 0·849–0·999], p=0·009).

major_points.text: GI disorders were the most frequent adverse reaction, occurring similarly in both groups.
major_points.quote: In both groups, gastrointestinal disorders were the most frequent adverse reaction (96 [3%] n-3 PUFA group vs 92 [3%] placebo group).

inclusion_criteria.text: Men and women aged 18 years or older with clinical evidence of heart failure of any cause, ESC-classified NYHA class II–IV.
inclusion_criteria.quote: Eligible patients were men and women aged 18 years or older, with clinical evidence of heart failure of any cause that was classiﬁed according to the European Society of Cardiology (ESC) guidelines as New York Heart Association (NYHA) class II–IV

inclusion_criteria.text: Left ventricular ejection fraction measured within 3 months before enrolment.
inclusion_criteria.quote: provided that they had had their LVEF measured within 3 months before enrolment.

inclusion_criteria.text: If LVEF was greater than 40%, at least one hospital admission for heart failure in the preceding year was required.
inclusion_criteria.quote: When LVEF was greater than 40%, the patient had to have been admitted at least once to hospital for heart failure in the preceding year to meet the inclusion criteria.

exclusion_criteria.text: Specific indication or contraindication to n-3 PUFA.

exclusion_criteria.text: Non-cardiac comorbidity unlikely compatible with sufficiently long follow-up (eg, cancer).
exclusion_criteria.quote: presence of any non-cardiac comorbidity (eg, cancer) that was unlikely to be compatible with a suﬃciently long follow-up;
